## jig v0.2.0-alpha.2

Names become verifiable claims. Nameservers sign attestations as COSE and bind every proof of
control to its action, and servers and clients now verify names against per-suffix delegations.
Servers sign a hash-chained record for every block they accept.

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking changes

- **jig-server parses its config strictly (#199).** Every table refuses unknown keys, and a key
  jig-server used to accept fails with a message saying to delete it. **A config copied from
  v0.2.0-alpha.1's `deploy/config.example.toml`, or written by v0.1.0-alpha.1's installer,
  fails to boot until its `[debug] admin_endpoints = false` line is deleted.**
  `dangerously_enable_v0_0_1_rest`,
  `[execution] pricing_enabled`, `[execution] cost_per_fuel` and `[storage]` are refused the
  same way.
- **Alias proofs are bound to their action (#210).** `POST /v1/register` and `/v1/renew` take a
  COSE proof of control that names the action, the nameserver's DID, the alias and the
  challenge; a signature over the bare challenge is refused. An alpha.1 CLI cannot register or
  renew against an alpha.2 nameserver. Attestations are COSE envelopes; responses carry
  `attestation`, `links`, `reachability` and unsigned `did`, `alias` and `valid_until` hints,
  and no longer `profile_ttl_seconds`. Rotation still takes signatures over the challenge from
  both keys.
- **A nameserver serves the suffixes its config names, and no default (#224).**
  `[v0_0_2.nameserver] alias_suffix` is replaced by the required list
  `[[v0_0_2.nameserver.alias_suffixes]]`; a config with neither, or with the old key, does not
  start. A nameserver set up from the deploy quickstart needs `/etc/jig/jig-nameserver.toml`
  naming its suffix (the unit sets `JIG_NS_CONFIG`). A single-label suffix needs
  `single_label_authority = true`. A DID holds one name per suffix: a second registration, or a
  rotation onto a DID that already holds one, gets 409 `DID_HOLDS_NAME`.
- **Servers in `nameserver` mode resolve names only through `[identity.delegations]` (#200).**
  Each suffix lists its `authorities` (the nameserver DIDs whose attestations count) and the
  `nameservers` to ask. A name under a suffix with no entry is refused. `trusted_nameservers`
  is no longer used, and the server warns at startup if it is set.
- **The CLI refuses plaintext servers that are not on its own machine (#142).** `jig` talks
  `http://` only to loopback; anything else needs TLS.
- **`jig ns resolve` prints only verified answers (#214).** The suffix needs a
  `[naming.delegations]` entry in `cli.toml`, or a DNS-rooted delegation at
  `https://<suffix>/.well-known/jig-ns-delegation`.
- **Handshake refusals and ingest records are COSE (#187).** Refusals are
  `jig-handshake-refusal-v2`, which an alpha.1 client cannot verify.

### What's new

- **Verified names.** Servers (#200) and clients (#201) accept an attestation only from an
  authority of the suffix's delegation, inside its validity window, and ask every listed
  nameserver; two answers naming different DIDs refuse the name. Both keep the attestations
  they act on.
- **Name pins.** `jig trust verify-name` pins a verified name's DID and refuses a changed one
  until `jig trust accept-name` moves the pin (#213).
- **Several suffixes per nameserver** (#224), each with its own registration policy (`open` or
  `closed`, minimum length, reserved names, an allowlist), `GET /v1/suffixes`, and
  `jig-nameserver keygen` for making the nameserver key offline.
- **Signed ingest records** (#161). The server signs a hash-chained record (`seq`, `prev`) for
  every block of a channel it holds, orders history by `seq`, and serves the records with
  history, on WebSocket block frames and at `GET /api/v1/channels/{slug}/records`.
- **Key links** are specified (JEP-0012, draft) and implemented as a library
  (`jig_core::key_link`, #235). Nothing carries them yet.

### Other changes

- **The nameserver needs no secret** (#192). `JIG_NS_SECRET` and the `[pow]` section went with
  the legacy proof-of-work routes; a config or environment that still sets them starts, and
  they are ignored.
- **The nameserver publishes the limits it enforces** (#197): `policy.alias_rate_limits` in
  `/.well-known/jig-ns` replaces `rate_limit`, and `[rate_limits]` and `JIG_NS_RATE_*` are
  ignored.
- **The v0.0.1 `jig.db` store is gone** (#196). jig-server opens only the derived
  `jig_v002.db`. An upgraded box keeps its old `jig.db`, unused; delete it once no backup needs
  it.
- **Backups include the nameserver** (#239): `jig-backup.sh` snapshots `nameserver_v002.db` and
  `nameserver_v002.key`, refuses a snapshot of the alias store without its key, and no longer
  copies `jig.db`.
- **The nameserver refuses `ns-attestation` blocks** (#224).

### Pending (not merged yet; move into the sections above as each lands)

- Breaking, #234: the mutual handshake. The welcome's signed bytes add `server_nonce` and
  `tls_exporter`, with no compatibility window. **jig-server must terminate TLS itself**: behind
  a TLS-terminating proxy the exporter is empty and every client refuses the server, so front
  it with TCP or SNI passthrough only.
- Breaking, #236: the `#jig/` channel prefix is reserved for the server; an existing channel
  there is moved aside at boot.
- Breaking, #237: the nameserver's `[federation]` section and its `JIG_NS_*` federation
  variables are removed, and ignored with a warning.
- Breaking, #242: a DID spelled any way but its canonical lowercase form is refused in signed
  objects.
- Breaking, #233: channel names get a canonical form.
- Change, #243: rotation keeps both keys when its outcome is unknown.
- New, #244: `jig_core::program`, the program manifest and program CID (JEP-0011 section 2), as
  a library.
- Change, #222: the runtime links one component linker per grant. A renderer whose grant names
  an import no host provides is refused at link time (`CapabilityDenied`), not when it calls the
  import.
- Lane A's step 6, when it opens.

### Known limitations

- **Clients do not check the ingest chain yet.** The records are signed and served, but no
  client verifies `seq` and `prev`, so omission and reordering are not yet detected (OP-06).
- **Only `jig trust verify-name` pins names.** `jig ns resolve` verifies but does not pin.
- **Rotation proofs are not bound** to the action, nameserver or alias (AB-01).
- **Identity keys are still not encrypted at rest.**

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NS-01 False or poisoned resolution | Servers and clients accept only attestations an authority of the suffix's delegation signed, inside their validity | Partial |
| NS-02 Equivocation | Resolvers refuse conflicting answers and keep the attestations they act on; there is no log | Partial |
| OP-08 Key substitution | `jig trust verify-name` pins names' DIDs; the CLI refuses remote plaintext | Partial |
| AB-01 Challenge replay | Register and renew proofs are bound to the action, nameserver and alias; rotate is not | Partial |
| TM-02 Self-asserted timestamps | History is ordered by the sequencer's signed `seq`, not authors' clocks | Partial |
| OP-06 Omission and reordering | The server signs a hash-chained record per block; clients do not check it yet | Partial |
| OP-03 Suite downgrade | The client refuses a restricted channel under a suite the operator can read | Partial |

Still open or accepted in this release, among others: OP-04 (metadata), OP-10 and AB-05 (Sybil
resistance), AB-06 (provable abuse in encrypted channels), and NS-03. The register lists them
all.
